name: controlled-bottleneck gate-capacity alternatives
description: An explicitly out-of-domain, uncalibrated structural exit-capacity sweep informed by the source-locked Wuppertal controlled-gate report.

factors.subject: entry_gate
factors.rationale: The alternatives are the locked adapter's per-run P05/P50/P95 observed passage-flow order statistics through the publisher-described fixed 0.5 m gate. They provide a disclosed structural bracket around the deliberately authored P50 baseline, not a fitted exit-capacity law.

references.citation: Adrian, J., Boltes, M., Holl, S., Sieben, A., & Seyfried, A. (2018). Crowds in front of bottlenecks from the perspective of physics and social psychology [data set]. Pedestrian Dynamics Data Archive. https://doi.org/10.34735/ped.2018.1
references.applicability: The source-locked Chiyoda adapter reports observed passage through the publisher-described 0.5 m controlled entry gate as explicitly bounded alternatives for structural exploration.
references.limitation: The source is a 2018 controlled university experiment with varying corridor width, priming, motivation, and participant counts. It is not a transit station, an evacuation, a validation of Chiyoda's token service rule, or a general exit-capacity law.

claim_boundary: This source-linked study only shows the deterministic reference runtime's response to explicit, out-of-domain gate-capacity alternatives. It does not estimate a station exit's capacity, calibrate the runtime, predict crowd queues, or support operational or safety claims.
